title: Character Encoding Detection and Superset Mapping
description: The cluster consists of two key components: `AutoDetectReader` and `CharsetSupersets`. `AutoDetectReader` reads from an input stream, automatically detects the character encoding, and handles Byte Order Marks (BOMs). It uses a `ServiceLoader` to load `EncodingDetector` implementations, enhancing flexibility. `CharsetSupersets` maps detected charsets to safer superset charsets, ensuring robust decoding. These components interact by `AutoDetectReader` using `CharsetSupersets` to select a superset charset when necessary. The architecture supports scalability and extensibility through dynamic loading of detectors and unmodifiable charset mappings. Technology Used: Java, `java.nio.charset`, `java.util`, and Apache Tika.

title: Character Encoding Detection System
description: This system consists of multiple detectors (`MetadataCharsetDetector`, `BOMDetector`, `OverrideEncodingDetector`) that implement the `EncodingDetector` interface to detect character encodings of documents. The `MetadataCharsetDetector` extracts charset information from metadata, while the `BOMDetector` identifies byte-order marks at the beginning of streams. The `OverrideEncodingDetector` always returns a specified charset. These detectors interact through the `EncodingResult` class, which encapsulates the detected charset, confidence, and evidence type. The system ensures high accuracy and reliability in encoding detection, supporting scalability and maintainability. Technology Used: Java, Apache Tika, Jackson.

title: Content Type Detection System
description: The Content Type Detection System is a modular and extensible framework for determining the media type of input streams. It consists of several detectors, including `CompositeDetector`, `NameDetector`, `MagicDetector`, `DefaultDetector`, `DefaultProbDetector`, and `OverrideDetector`. These components work together to provide a robust detection pipeline. The `CompositeDetector` orchestrates the process by combining multiple detectors, while `NameDetector` and `MagicDetector` use file names and magic bytes, respectively, to infer media types. `DefaultDetector` and `DefaultProbDetector` provide default and probabilistic detection, respectively, and `OverrideDetector` allows for user-specified overrides. The system ensures high accuracy, flexibility, and performance, achieving scalability and maintainability. It leverages Java, Apache Tika, and service provider interfaces (SPI) for dynamic loading of detectors.

title: Character Encoding Detection System
description: The system consists of a `CompositeEncodingDetector` that aggregates multiple `EncodingDetector` instances, including a `MetaEncodingDetector`, to determine the most appropriate encoding for input streams. The `EncodingDetectorContext` manages and organizes the results from base detectors, providing a structured way to store and access encoding detection outcomes. The `MetaEncodingDetector` arbitrates among the collected results to select the final encoding. The `DefaultEncodingDetector` initializes and sorts the detectors using a service provider mechanism. This architecture ensures high accuracy and flexibility in encoding detection, supporting both first-match-wins and collect-all modes. Quality attributes include scalability, modularity, and extensibility. Technology used includes Java, service loaders, and TikaInputStream for input handling.

title: Content Detection and Type Identification System
description: This cluster comprises several detectors for identifying file types and content. The `ZeroSizeFileDetector` identifies zero-length files, returning a specific media type. The `DetectHelper` optimizes large file detection by reading limited portions. The `TypeDetector` uses metadata to determine content types, defaulting to `application/octet-stream` if no valid type is found. The `EmptyDetector` always returns `application/octet-stream`, while the `FileCommandDetector` leverages the Linux `file` command for MIME type detection, falling back to `application/octet-stream` if the command is unavailable. These components interact through the Apache Tika framework, ensuring efficient and accurate content detection. Quality attributes include performance optimization, robustness, and fallback mechanisms. Technology used includes Java, Apache Tika, and the Linux `file` command.

title: Neural Network Model Detection System
description: This cluster comprises components for constructing, managing, and utilizing neural network models to detect media types. The `NNTrainedModelBuilder` constructs `NNTrainedModel` instances, setting up the neural network architecture and parameters. The `NNTrainedModel` class implements prediction logic using sigmoid functions. The `TrainedModelDetector` abstract class and its subclass `NNExampleModelDetector` handle media type detection by converting input streams into byte frequency histograms and predicting media types using registered models. The system achieves scalability through modular design and security by encapsulating sensitive operations. It uses Java for implementation, leveraging Apache Tika for stream handling.

title: Text Analysis and Detection System
description: This cluster comprises two Java classes, `TextStatistics` and `TextDetector`, which work together to analyze and detect the characteristics of text streams. `TextStatistics` computes byte histograms and checks for ASCII and UTF-8 encoding, while `TextDetector` uses these statistics to determine if a document is a text document based on control byte presence and character distribution. The system ensures efficient and accurate text detection, supporting scalability and reliability in text processing applications. Technology Used: Java, TikaInputStream, Metadata, ParseContext.

title: XML Root Element Extractor
description: The `XmlRootExtractor` class extracts the root element's namespace URI and local name from XML files. It processes both byte arrays and input streams, with robust error handling for malformed or truncated XML. The main method, `extractRootElement`, parses the XML and retries if a `MalformedCharException` occurs. A nested `ExtractorHandler` class captures the root element using a SAX parser, ensuring efficient parsing by aborting once the root is found. This component enhances security and reliability through exception handling. Technology Used: Java, SAX Parser.

title: Apache Tika Media Type Detection and Parsing
description: This cluster comprises two packages within the Apache Tika project: `org.apache.tika.parser` and `org.apache.tika.detect`. The `parser` package handles the extraction of metadata and structured content from various document types, while the `detect` package focuses on identifying the media type of files or data streams. Both packages interact by using file streams, byte arrays, or file paths as inputs and producing structured content and metadata or MIME type strings as outputs. The cluster leverages Apache Tika's core utilities for file I/O and content processing, ensuring scalability and robustness. It uses aQute Bnd for versioning and OSGi bundle management.

title: Tika Parsing Architecture
description: This cluster comprises a suite of Java classes and interfaces for content parsing and encoding detection, leveraging the Apache Tika library. **Components and Interactions:** The `Parser` interface defines the contract for parsing documents, while `AbstractParser` and `DelegatingParser` provide base implementations for backward compatibility and delegation, respectively. `DefaultParser` aggregates multiple parsers using a service loader, enabling dynamic parsing of various media types. `AbstractEncodingDetectorParser` adds encoding detection capabilities, and `RenderingParser` allows for content rendering. `ParseContext` manages context information, and `EmptyParser` handles unsupported formats by producing an empty document. **Quality Attributes:** The architecture supports extensibility, modularity, and backward compatibility, ensuring robust and flexible parsing. **Technology Used:** Java, Apache Tika, ServiceLoader, XHTMLContentHandler.

title: External Process Parsing System
description: The External Process Parsing System consists of three core components: `AbstractExternalProcessParser`, `ExternalParserConfig`, and `ExternalParser`. `AbstractExternalProcessParser` manages external processes, ensuring they are properly terminated upon JVM exit. `ExternalParserConfig` provides immutable configurations for external parsers, including MIME type support, command-line arguments, and output handlers. `ExternalParser` executes external processes to parse documents, using the configuration to handle outputs and extract content and metadata. This system ensures robust process management, secure configuration, and flexible parsing capabilities. Quality attributes include high reliability, security, and configurability. Technology used includes Java, Apache Tika, and JSON for configuration.

title: Document Parsing and Detection System
description: This cluster comprises components for automatic document type detection and parsing, with a focus on handling encrypted documents and error management. The `AutoDetectParser` uses a `Detector` to identify document types and selects the appropriate parser, while `ParsingIntent` signals the intent to parse. `SimplePasswordProvider` and `PasswordProvider` interfaces manage passwords for encrypted documents. `AutoDetectParserConfig` allows configuring parsing behavior, such as handling zero-byte files. `ErrorParser` ensures that unsupported document types trigger exceptions. Quality attributes include flexibility, security, and robust error handling. Technology used includes Java, Apache Tika, and the Singleton pattern.

title: Content Parsing and Metadata Management System
description: This cluster implements a flexible and extensible content parsing system using the Apache Tika library. **Components and Interactions**: The `ParserDecorator` class decorates parsers to filter media types, while `AbstractMultipleParser` serves as a base for parsers that use multiple sub-parsers, merging their results. `SupplementingParser` and `FallbackParser` extend this base, with `SupplementingParser` merging metadata from multiple parsers and `FallbackParser` attempting parsing with multiple parsers sequentially. `CompositeParser` selects the appropriate parser based on content type, supporting fallbacks. **Quality Attributes**: Achieves high flexibility, robustness, and maintainability. **Technology Used**: Java, Apache Tika.

title: Content Parsing and Decryption System
description: This system consists of three core components: `ParsingReader`, `CryptoParser`, and `NetworkParser`. `ParsingReader` reads and parses binary streams into a character stream using a background thread and a pipe mechanism. `CryptoParser` decrypts encrypted documents and delegates further parsing to another parser, ensuring secure content handling. `NetworkParser` fetches and parses content from network resources, supporting various protocols and media types, and executes parsing tasks in a separate thread to prevent blocking. The system achieves high security, scalability, and non-blocking I/O operations. Technologies used include Java, Apache Tika, and standard cryptographic libraries.

title: Document Parsing and Metadata Management System
description: This cluster comprises components that facilitate the parsing of complex documents and management of metadata. The `RecursiveParserWrapper` handles recursive parsing of container documents and their embedded resources, managing paths and exceptions. The `ParseRecord` tracks parsing depth, exceptions, warnings, and metadata to prevent resource exhaustion and ensure compliance with limits. The `ParserPostProcessor` enhances parser output by extracting and setting metadata for full text, summary, and outlinks. The `StatefulParser` manages parser state, ensuring correct handling of inline content like OCR. Together, these components achieve robust, scalable, and secure document parsing with detailed metadata extraction. Technology Used: Java, Apache Tika.

title: Text Parsing and Configuration Management
description: The cluster consists of two components: `RegexCaptureParser` and `RegexCaptureParserConfig`. `RegexCaptureParser` parses text content using regular expressions defined in `RegexCaptureParserConfig`. It reads an input stream, matches patterns, and updates metadata. Optionally, it writes parsed content to a `ContentHandler`. `RegexCaptureParserConfig` manages configuration settings, including capture and match mappings and a flag for content writing. This setup ensures flexibility and configurability. Quality attributes include modularity and maintainability. Technologies used include Java, Apache Tika, and standard Java libraries.
